reviewedExecution.approvedForm: Run the exact committed file once, unmodified, as a single explicit BEGIN..COMMIT transaction, e.g. psql "$DB" -X -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f supabase/migrations/20261018063016_question_group_identity.sql (no -1, the file has its own BEGIN/COMMIT). Verify the file SHA immediately before running.
notApproved: supabase db push or any blanket schema push
editing, splitting or re-running parts of the SQL
running when a fresh pre-run catalog read differs from db-catalog-before (re-review)
reviewedExecution.ifAborted: Any RAISE aborts the whole transaction; nothing is applied. Do not retry with altered SQL; bring the new catalog for review.

reviewNotes: Additive: one nullable text column, two plain indexes, one trigger function, one BEFORE UPDATE trigger. No data rewrite.

ACL step requires exactly the two owner-issued non-grantable INSERT/UPDATE grants per browser role, revokes only those and regrants them as column grants over every pre-existing column; then asserts via has_column_privilege (covers PUBLIC and inherited membership) that the new key is not writable and every old column still is. SELECT/DELETE/TRUNCATE/REFERENCES/TRIGGER/MAINTAIN, service_role, owner, RLS and policies are untouched.

Trigger compares the 18 identity fields named in plan section on identity (7 metadata, content/answer/solution, 6 figure fields, external_id, question_type) and nulls the key even when the same UPDATE supplies one. Key-only/eligibility/timestamp updates keep it. SECURITY INVOKER, search_path fixed to pg_catalog, public. Revoking EXECUTE does not affect firing (PostgreSQL checks trigger-function EXECUTE only at CREATE TRIGGER).
Trigger name sorts between problem_code_freeze and registered_problem_outer_wall; it only clears NEW.question_group_key so it does not interfere with code freeze or the outer wall.

Locking: ADD COLUMN takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE held to COMMIT, including two non-concurrent index builds over an all-NULL column; lock_timeout 3s and statement_timeout 30s bound the stall. Brief read blocking on public.problem is expected.
Independently ran src/__tests__/unit/questionIdentityDdl.test.ts against this exact file (PGlite): 32/32 passed. PGlite does not prove production role membership or concurrent locking.
requiredAfterRun: Post-DDL read-only role catalog: column present and NULL everywhere; anon/authenticated have no table-level INSERT/UPDATE, have column INSERT/UPDATE on every old column, none on question_group_key; SELECT/DELETE etc. unchanged; service_role unchanged; RLS still false, policies 0; trigger and function present with EXECUTE not granted to PUBLIC/anon/authenticated; index list.

Applying via psql does not record the version in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations; record or reconcile it explicitly so a later supabase db push does not try to re-run it (it would fail on ADD COLUMN, not silently double-apply).
knownLimitationsOutsideScope: Future columns added to public.problem will not be writable by anon/authenticated unless granted explicitly, because the table-level write grant is now column-scoped.
Pre-existing: RLS is disabled and browser roles keep DELETE/TRUNCATE on public.problem. Not widened or narrowed here; worth a separate review.
Privileged direct SQL can still set a key without proof (by design, plan); only the protected operator/loader may do so.
dependency: Independent of the 17-row repair outcome. The Gate 2 backfill manifest must be prepared after the DDL and after whatever repair state is actually in the DB.
